clue.text: Witty saying has some point with animals

parts.note: E, east, is one point of the compass
a pig is one farm animal
a ram is another farm animal, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A clever quip involving a point made with animals, like a fable's moral.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'animals' does double duty as a pair of farmyard creatures; 'some point' is any compass point, here east.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short pointed remark, typically clever and memorable.

clue.text: Last character leaves Cornish town in humiliation

indicators.note: the letter that leaves the town's name is taken out of it

parts.note: Penzance is a town at the far western tip of Cornwall
Z is the last character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone humiliated quits a town in Cornwall at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: PENZANCE is a seaside town in Cornwall, England; remove Z, the alphabet's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-abasement undertaken as punishment, close to humiliation.

clue.text: Look back in Middle Ages for capital savers

indicators.note: the turned word is set within the middle letters of the next word
the middle letters of the word Ages are taken, dropping its ends
back says the word for look is written in the reverse direction

parts.note: to look is to see

explanation.surface: Glancing back at medieval history for those who saved a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle Ages' looks like the historical period, but means GE, the middle of AGES; 'back' turns SEE into EES, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says cackling geese warned the Romans of a Gaulish attack on the Capitol, saving the city.

clue.text: His is a searching examination, by all accounts

definitions.text: His is a searching examination, by all accounts

parts.words: His is a searching examination, by all accounts
parts.note: by all accounts reads as reportedly, but literally means every set of financial books is examined by this person

explanation.surface: Someone renowned for thorough scrutiny, or so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examines a company's financial accounts closely and independently.

clue.text: Enigmatic, keen and in charge, set about exercising

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so two pieces surround the exercise one

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry
PT, physical training, is exercising

explanation.surface: A mysterious, eager boss who has started doing exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: CRY and IC go 'about' PT: CRY-PT-IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cryptic is obscure or puzzling in meaning, like an enigma.

clue.text: Brush off and polish again

definitions.meaning: to brush off someone is to snub or ... them
to buff is to polish, so ... is polishing once more

explanation.definitionFit: Rebuff means reject curtly, and split as re-buff it means shine up again.

clue.text: Dine with Ralph, prepared to flirt

indicators.note: prepared as food is, the letters of the two words are made up anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dinner date with Ralph, ready for some flirtation.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual love affairs or flirt with many partners.

clue.text: The way in which a French painter finally got the point

indicators.note: the point comes at the end, after the painter

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Describes how an artist from France eventually understood what was meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally got' places compass point S last, after INGRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act or means of entering, an entrance.

clue.text: Espy an admirer, perhaps the answer to this?

definitions.text: Espy an admirer, perhaps the answer to this?

indicators.note: perhaps signals the three words could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lonely girl spotting a suitor might see this as her wish granted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Maiden's Prayer is a once-popular 19th-century piano piece by Tekla Bądarzewska; a maiden's prayer might well be to spot an admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden praying for a suitor would be answered by spying one, so the clue describes it whole.

clue.text: Stake for backing a mount

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the mountain's name is read backwards

parts.note: Etna is a volcanic mountain in Sicily

explanation.surface: A bet placed on a horse, a mount, to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' suggests a horse in a betting surface, but it is Mount ETNA, which 'backing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put into the pot before the cards are dealt in poker.

clue.text: Put up defence and tie game

parts.note: a tied match is a draw
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A team defends stoutly and the match ends level.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's raisable bridge over the moat is a defence that is literally put up.

clue.text: Fashionable school for cricket, say?

parts.note: in means fashionable
a school of thought is a sect

explanation.surface: A trendy school for playing cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' looks like the bat-and-ball game, but here it is the chirping creature; 'say?' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is one example of a six-legged invertebrate of this class.

clue.text: It's discharged in battle during action

indicators.note: during says one piece occurs within the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
a fray is a battle or brawl

explanation.surface: A soldier being discharged from service mid-combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' suggests a soldier or a gun, but here it means paid off, as a debt is.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay or settle them, so a discharged debt is defrayed.

clue.text: Instructing or admonishing

definitions.meaning: teaching by giving talks to a class
telling someone off at tedious length

explanation.definitionFit: Lecturing means both giving formal teaching talks and scolding someone at length.

clue.text: Bound to be in step — and rated highly

indicators.note: says the first piece is to be placed inside the second

parts.note: a tread is a step, as on a staircase
bound to happen means sure to happen

explanation.surface: Someone certain to keep in step with others and held in high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like a leap, but here means certain, as in bound to happen; 'to be in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is valued greatly and cherished.

clue.text: Edits a translation that is in Latin

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A translator revises Latin text.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is the Latin phrase abbreviated i.e., meaning 'that is'.

clue.text: Music of the Depression?

parts.note: the Depression suggests the 1930s slump, but read as low mood it describes melancholy song

explanation.surface: Songs from the Great Depression era.
explanation.definitionFit: Blues is a sad musical genre, and the blues is a state of low spirits.

clue.text: Cave used as an observation post

definitions.meaning: cave is Latin for beware, school slang for 'watch out'
a place from which a watch is kept

explanation.definitionFit: Cave was British schoolboy slang shouted to warn others, meaning beware; an observation post is also a watch station.

clue.text: Void contest?

parts.note: void suggests an annulled match, but read as outer space it describes a competition to reach it

explanation.surface: A competition declared null and void.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cold War rivalry between the USA and USSR to explore space is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivalry between superpowers over exploration of the cosmos, literally a contest about the void.

clue.text: Pipe of pipes

parts.note: one particular pipe belonging to a set of pipes, the melody tube of a bagpipe

explanation.surface: The principal pipe among many.
explanation.definitionFit: The chanter is the melody pipe of a bagpipe, played with the fingers.

clue.text: Voting against, told to go and vote for

parts.note: the cons are those against, as in pros and cons
sent means told to go, dispatched

explanation.surface: Opponents who are dismissed then vote in favour.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent is to agree to something, giving it approval.

clue.text: Wild herb found around Virginia

indicators.note: the herb is found placed around the state abbreviation

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A herb growing in the wild in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found around' is the container signal; 'Wild' leads the clue as the definition, not a description of the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage means fierce, untamed and uncivilised, just as wild can.

clue.text: Saw baton wielded in Africa

indicators.note: wielded as a stick is waved, the letters are swung into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone saw a conductor's baton being waved on an African visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked country of southern Africa.

clue.text: Display by top-class band

parts.note: A1 means top-class, written with the figure one as the letter I
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A first-rate musical group putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks musical, but it is a ring; A1 is a mark of excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: Airing means a public display or expression, as of views or clothes.

clue.text: Being sorry, one called out

annotationWithheld.why: Being sorry, one called out (5): RUING looks like I (one) in RUNG (called), but no clue word signals the insertion and 'out' has no job

clue.text: How people may call us in explosive competition

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
the way people address us is by our name

explanation.surface: Being addressed by name at a fiery sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OUR NAME inside TNT: T-OURNAME-NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a series of contests between competitors.

clue.text: Perfect but inconclusive thought

indicators.note: inconclusive means lacking its end, so the last letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A theory that is flawless yet leads to no conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEAL loses its last letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion formed in the mind.

clue.text: It's used to compose pieces of music

definitions.meaning: a study is a room used for writing; the plural answer is these rooms
..., or études, are instrumental pieces for practice

explanation.definitionFit: A study is a writing room; studies are also musical exercises called études.

clue.text: Ship's sails etc split a lot

indicators.note: the word for a lot is split open so the sails go in

parts.note: one's fate is one's lot in life
a ship's rig is its sails, masts and so on

explanation.surface: A ship's sails and rigging torn badly in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' is the container signal; 'a lot' looks like 'many' but means one's destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship.
